premises.text: Existing recommendation systems rely on stranger reviews, non-personalized averages, and widespread fake reviews
premises.evidence_span: all of these systems are dependent on giving you reviews and recommendations from strangers

premises.text: LiveStar surfaces aggregated recommendations from professional critics
premises.evidence_span: recommended restaurant according to the top 12 critics in San Francisco

premises.text: LiveStar gathers friend recommendations, including Q&A via email, SMS, and Facebook with pre-populated surveys for non-users
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar has a Q&A feature that lets me send a question, a request for some recommendations to friends

premises.text: An algorithm measures taste similarity and surfaces recommendations from people with matching taste
premises.evidence_span: LiveStar algorithmically measures your taste and then compares it to other people

premises.text: One app covers restaurants, on-menu items, music, and movies as a multi-category destination
premises.evidence_span: you can go to LiveStar for restaurants, what to eat when you're at the restaurant, what music to listen to, and what movie to watch

domains.name: trusted critic friend and taste sources

value.text: Fast access to high-quality personalized recommendations from trusted sources
value.evidence_span: give you access to high-quality reviews from trusted sources

causal_links.evidence_span: Clearly, the existing solutions are broken
provides fast access to high quality sources across a range of common real world scenarios
We're a one-stop destination, and we're constantly adding new categories

notes: Stranger/average/fake review issues folded as one problem set (§4.1.6). Critic, friend(+Q&A cascade), and similar-taste sources kept as distinct mechanisms within one trusted-sources domain. Keyword refine and menu-item ranking treated as UI cascade of those sources. Date-story framing not coded as separate premises.
